lines_of_business: All lines of business unless noted in Program Exceptions
sections_in_order: Description (with Summary and Analysis of Evidence)
criteria_location: There are NO clinical medical-necessity criteria. The Position Statement (p.3-4 of 10) has two sentences: balloon dilation is integral to FESS when done at the same time and not separately reimbursable; implantable sinus devices are experimental or investigational. The only 'requirements' are a documentation list and LOINC table in Billing/Coding.
procedures_covered: Implantable sinus devices / steroid-eluting stents (Propel, MicroFlow Spacer): investigational
Sinuva: redirected to a drugs policy (09-J0000-38)

logic.top_level: other (bundling rule plus investigational list; no criteria tree)
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: None; one blanket investigational statement for implantable devices: 'considered experimental or investigational for all indications'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: The use of an FDA approved catheter-based inflatable device ... in the treatment of sinusitis is considered integral to the traditional nasal/sinus endoscopic surgery or functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) when performed at the same time and is not separately reimbursable.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: States a payment rule only. It does not say whether stand-alone balloon dilation is medically necessary, not necessary, or covered under other criteria. Silence is not a coverage decision; a checker cannot tell if stand-alone dilation is approvable.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Balloon sinuplasty is proposed as an alternative to endoscopic sinus surgery for individuals with chronic sinusitis who fail medical management (e.g., mucolytic, decongestant (oral and topical), antibiotic therapy).
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: A descriptive sentence naming medical management examples that looks like a criterion; it is in the Description, not the Position Statement.

extraction_hazards: Long evidence summary (Castro 2021, Kutluhan 2020, Han and Kern 2019) mentions chronic rhinosinusitis, failed medical management and CT scores, none of which are criteria.
LOINC documentation table is flattened into columns; the 'Physician history and physical' row appears twice (duplicate).
Description sentence 'fail medical management (e.g., mucolytic, decongestant ...)' reads like a criterion.
Reference list is 60+ items with a missing item 20 merge (two references fused).
interesting_structures: A coverage guideline whose position statement is a reimbursement/bundling rule rather than medical-necessity criteria.
Documentation requirements expressed as LOINC codes with time-frame modifier codes: machine-oriented, aimed at electronic attachments.
Implantable steroid-eluting devices declared investigational in the same document; Sinuva routed to a drug policy.
Policy title says 'and Implantable Devices'; the file stem is truncated.

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = clean, 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: There is no criteria tree to build. The checker would need to treat the policy as: stand-alone dilation has no stated criteria (so it cannot be evaluated), concurrent-with-FESS dilation is bundled, devices are investigational. A claims-bundling rule is not a chart-testable criterion.
